q: You enable UniForm on a 2 TB Delta table. How much extra data storage does it roughly need?
o: Another 2 TB for the Iceberg copy
About 1 TB, because Iceberg compresses better
Only small metadata files: the Parquet data files are shared
Nothing, Iceberg reads the Delta log directly
e: UniForm writes Iceberg metadata (JSON and Avro) that points to the same Parquet files. The data is not copied.

q: Why does UniForm turn on column mapping?
o: Iceberg identifies columns by field id, so every column needs a stable id
To make queries faster
Because Iceberg cannot read Parquet
To encrypt the column names
e: Iceberg schemas use field ids. Column mapping gives each Delta column an id and a physical name, which also makes renames metadata-only.

q: An existing table has deletion vectors. What is the recommended way to enable Iceberg reads with Iceberg v2?
o: Set only `delta.universalFormat.enabledFormats`
Drop and recreate the table
Run VACUUM first
`REORG TABLE t APPLY (UPGRADE UNIFORM(ICEBERG_COMPAT_VERSION = 2))`
e: REORG rewrites the files that carry deletion vectors, disables them, and sets the UniForm properties in one step.

q: An INSERT into a UniForm table commits Delta version 12. When do Iceberg clients see the new rows?
o: Never: Iceberg clients only see version 0
After the Iceberg metadata for version 12 is generated, shortly after the commit
Only after OPTIMIZE
In the same instant, inside the same commit file
e: Iceberg metadata is generated asynchronously after the Delta commit. DESCRIBE EXTENDED shows the last converted Delta version.

q: An external open-source Spark must read a UniForm table. What does it need?
o: Direct write access to the table folder and the Delta jars
A copy of the table exported to CSV
The Iceberg Spark runtime and a REST catalog pointing to the Unity Catalog Iceberg endpoint, with a principal that has SELECT
Nothing: every Spark reads Iceberg by default
e: Iceberg clients use the Unity Catalog Iceberg REST catalog. Unity Catalog checks the usual privileges and hands out the metadata location.
